subject.title: Session files should never be deleted — rename .deleted.* to .archived.*

question: Should OpenClaw replace the shipped `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` session archive convention and current physical purge behavior with a permanent archive naming or directory model, and what migration/purge policy should existing users get?
rationale: Current source proves the reported behavior remains, but choosing suffix names, archive storage layout, compatibility handling, and whether physical purge remains allowed is a shipped storage and product contract decision.

options.title: Adopt archive terminology with migration
options.body: Rename or move future retained transcripts, add doctor/backfill handling for old `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` artifacts, and keep physical purge behind an explicit documented retention setting.

options.title: Keep behavior and clarify docs
options.body: Leave current suffixes and cleanup behavior intact, but document that `.deleted.*` means detached until retention or disk-budget cleanup removes it.

options.title: Split naming from purge policy
options.body: Use the narrower semantics issue for suffix/config terminology and track the no-physical-delete rule as a separate durability decision.

recommendation.title: Adopt archive terminology with migration
recommendation.body: Rename or move future retained transcripts, add doctor/backfill handling for old `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` artifacts, and keep physical purge behind an explicit documented retention setting.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session product/docs work makes this the best available owner for choosing the user-facing lifecycle contract.
